To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucocorticoid (DEX; 1 μM) inhibits the expression of cell adhesion molecule on human T‐lymphocytes, which are stimulated by plastic‐bound anti‐CD3 (OKT3).
glucocorticoid treatment of lymphocytes does not result in an increase of the glucocorticoids‐induced protein, lipocortin, but rather results in a decrease in the expression of this protein.
glucocorticoids inhibit lymphocyte adhesion events through mechanisms independent of lipocortin‐1 (LC1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms involved in the anti‐inflammation effects of the glucocorticoids, in particular, the role of LC1.
the role of glucocorticoid receptors (GRs) in the regulation of cell‐to‐cell adhesion events in the immune response.
the mechanisms of action of glucocorticoid drugs and the role of the glucocorticoids in inflammatory disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucocorticoids inhibit lymphocyte adhesion events through mechanisms which do not involve LC1.
LC1 has a minor, if any, role in mediating the anti‐inflammation properties of glucocorticoid.
glucocorticoids exert multiple effects on leucocytes, which include inhibition of CAM expression, but the role of LC1 is unclear and may not be a primary event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glucocorticoids inhibit lymphocyte adhesion by a direct effect on CAM expression and that LC1 does not appear to be involved.
the anti‐inflammation effect of glucocorticoid is mainly through the inhibition of the expression of adhesion molecules on leucocytes and endothelial cells, which is independent of lipocortin.
the anti‐inﬂammatory effects of glucocorti-coids on cell adhesion events are not mediated by lip-cortin 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LC1 is not a mediator of the glucocorticoids anti‐inflammatory actions on lymphocyte adhesions.
LC1 is a glucocorticoid target gene but does not mediate glucocorticoid effects on lymphocyte CAM expression or intercellular adhesion.
glucocorticoids inhibit the expression of CAM on the surface of lymphocytes, and the inhibition is not mediated by LC-1.
